transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what made me come in is... I've been having this issue where after work or class, I’ll sit down with my laptop and just end up eating a really large amount of food. Like, I'll eat an entire takeout meal, plus chips, sweets, and just whatever snacks I happen to have in my desk drawer. 

It ends up being way more than I ever planned to eat when I sat down. And honestly, it's a lot more than I’d ever eat if anyone else was around.
Do you think you eat this large amount of food because you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset after work or class?

I'm not really sure if it's tied to a specific feeling like that. I just... I get home, open my laptop, and start eating. I haven't really noticed if I'm stressed or upset when it happens, it just kind of happens.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those occasions?

No, not really. Once I start, it's like... I can't stop. It feels like I'm just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Even while I'm sitting there thinking, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you're not even enjoying this anymore... I just keep eating anyway.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these eating episodes?

Yeah, I definitely do. After it's all over and the food is gone, I just feel... really bad about myself. I feel guilty for spending the money, for eating so much, and honestly, just ashamed that I can't seem to control it. It's a pretty terrible feeling.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen?

Um, I actually looked back through my journal and my food delivery charges recently to check. It's been happening most weeks since the restructuring started at work. Usually it's more than once a week, so... it's definitely not just a here and there kind of thing.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these episodes?

Like I mentioned a few minutes ago, no, I really don't have any control. It goes back to that feeling of just watching myself do it. My brain is telling me to stop, reminding me about my budget reports and work, but my hands just keep reaching for more food anyway. It's like I'm completely on autopilot once I start.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly during these episodes?

I'm not really sure, honestly. Um, since I feel like I'm on autopilot during it, I don't really pay attention to how fast I'm chewing or swallowing. I just haven't really noticed my speed, so I couldn't say for sure.
Do you usually eat this large amount of food over a short period of time, like within an hour or less?

I'm really not sure about the exact timeframe. Um, since I kind of zone out like I mentioned, I just completely lose track of time. I don't really look at the clock when it's happening, so I couldn't tell you if it's all within an hour or if it takes longer than that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight due to these episodes of eating large amounts of food?

I haven't really noticed any major changes, to be honest. I don't really weigh myself very often, so I don't have a specific number or anything to give you. Um, my clothes still seem to fit about the same, so... yeah, I just haven't really tracked it or noticed a significant difference either way.
Do you usually eat these large amounts of food alone, without others present?

Yeah, I do. Um, I actually wait until my roommate is out of the apartment, or I'll wait until my family has gone to bed. I'm just really embarrassed for anyone to see how much I can eat. During the day, I act so put-together and, like, health-conscious around everyone, so... I really don't want anyone to see me doing that. So I definitely make sure I'm alone.
Do you feel anxious or stressed right before you start eating this large amount of food?

Um, no, I wouldn't really say so. I haven't noticed feeling particularly anxious or stressed right before it happens. I don't really know exactly what sets it off, to be honest, but I don't think it's tied to feeling stressed out right in that moment.
Do you criticize yourself after these eating episodes, beyond just feeling guilty or ashamed?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely feel guilty and embarrassed, like I said, but I don't really sit there and, like, beat myself up or criticize myself beyond that. It's more just a general feeling of shame, but not really any specific self-criticism.
Do you enjoy the taste of the food while you're eating during these episodes?
Um, I'm not really sure. I don't think I even really notice the taste, to be honest. I'm usually just eating so fast that I don't really pay attention to whether I'm actually enjoying it or not.
Do you think there are times when you use food as a way to cope with emotions or escape from stress?

Um, no, I don't really think so. I mean, I know some people eat when they're sad or stressed out, but I haven't really noticed that being the case for me. Like I was saying earlier, I don't really feel stressed right before it happens, so... yeah, it doesn't really feel like I'm using it as a coping mechanism or an escape. It just sort of happens.
Have these episodes of eating large amounts of food interfered with your daily life, work, or relationships in any significant way?

Yeah, it has. Um, mostly with my social life, I guess. I've actually been avoiding plans with my friends and family, especially things like cooking nights. I just get really worried that they'll somehow notice or figure out how much I've been eating in private. So... yeah, outside of work and school, I've definitely been a lot more isolated lately because I just stay home instead to avoid it.
Do you feel like you're eating because you're hungry or do you not really feel hungry when these episodes start?

No, I don't really feel hungry. A lot of the time, it actually starts right after I've already had dinner. I know I'm not physically hungry at all, but... my mind just feels restless, I guess. So I still end up going back to the kitchen or I'll even order more food, even though I literally just ate.
Do you feel full at any point during these episodes of eating large amounts of food?

Yeah, I do. But I usually keep going way past just feeling regular full. By the end of it, I'm so full that my stomach actually feels tight under my work pants. It gets to the point where I just have to sit there for a while once I stop, because if I try moving around or bending over, it literally makes me feel sick. So, yeah, I definitely feel full, but it's a really uncomfortable kind of full.
Do you ever experience any physical symptoms, such as nausea or stomach pain, after one of these eating episodes?

Um, well, like I said, I definitely feel uncomfortably full, and moving around makes me feel a bit sick, but I wouldn't say I get actual nausea or stomach pain. It's more just that really tight, stretched feeling from eating too much.
